workload: one exact-response full turn per fresh native primary session

suffix_control.interpretation: The control only changes session-start work; later-turn prompt-hook time remains unchanged.

microbenchmark.interpretation: Combining the three jq reads is a small local optimization. It does not explain the 1.1 second session hook gap.

interpretation: Measured. The primer control reduces fresh full-turn command time by 891 ms on average, a 17.0 percent paired reduction in this eight-pair probe.
Measured. The sessionStart hook reduction is stable at about 1.14 seconds per fresh session.
Measured. Later suffix turns show no reliable reduction because the primer runs only at session start.
Inferred. The safe optimization is an explicit runner control, not a global profile change. It keeps the other lifecycle hooks active.

Exploratory. The exact paired sign-flip p value is 0.015625, but the sample uses one model, one repository, one task shape, and eight pairs. Treat it as evidence for this control, not a general product guarantee.
limitations: The two arms ran in alternating fresh processes, not in a randomized multi-day production sample.
The primer control is an existing Ripwire control arm. It suppresses guidance context, so task-quality equivalence still needs a tool-using workload.
The jq microbenchmark measures field extraction only and does not modify the external Ripwire hook.
